setup.description: Create a feature branch on the DataCopilot repo (213) for eval runs. Pass the branch ID to each eval prompt.
setup.command: dxs source branch create --repo 213 --title "form-creator-eval-{timestamp}" --description "Temporary branch for form-creator skill evals"

evals.name: dialog-input-collector
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: our shipments grid needs a row action that opens a dialog where the user types a hold reason and picks a hold-until date, then hands both values back to the grid flow so it can update the row. Create the form (reference name eval_shipment_hold_form) and write the exact grid-side flow code that opens the dialog and consumes the result — including what the grid flow should do when the user closes the dialog without confirming.
evals.expected_output: A validated and upserted form (cti 5) whose confirm flow populates outParams (including is_confirmed) before $form.close(), plus caller-side dialog-opener code using $shell.<Package>.open<referenceName>Dialog with snake_case preserved and an explicit cancel branch for undefined outParams.
expectations: A form body is created with configurationTypeId 5 and referenceName eval_shipment_hold_form (snake_case, ending in _form)
The confirm flow assigns $form.outParams.<id> values BEFORE calling $form.close()
The form emits an explicit is_confirmed boolean outParam so callers can distinguish confirm from cancel

The grid-side opener code uses $shell.<Package>.open<referenceName>Dialog(...) with the snake_case referenceName preserved inside the method name (e.g. openeval_shipment_hold_formDialog — NOT camelCased like openEvalShipmentHoldFormDialog)
The <Package> segment in the dialog-open call is the target form's package (the package the form was created in), not a grid/caller-specific package

The caller-side code handles the cancel path explicitly — it notes that closing without confirm resolves the promise with undefined outParam fields and branches on is_confirmed (it does not treat undefined outParams as a confirm with empty values)
All new param ids are snake_case (e.g. hold_reason, hold_until, is_confirmed — no camelCase param ids)
No outParam that is written only on the confirm branch is declared required: true (the type contract must match the cancel close path too)
The form's description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains a 'dxs configuration validate form' command run before 'dxs configuration upsert form'

evals.name: validate-then-confirm-gating
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create a form eval_transfer_qty_form that collects a source location code (text), a destination location code (text), and a quantity (number). The Confirm button must stay disabled until all three are filled in and quantity is greater than zero; if source equals destination, show an error on both location fields. On confirm, return all three values to the caller and close.
evals.expected_output: A form whose confirm-button gating lives in onFormValidateFlowConfig + a validation flow that sets $form.toolbar.confirm.control.readOnly and pushes $validation.fieldErrors, with all flow-id references resolving and the full validate/upsert lifecycle.
expectations: Confirm-button gating is implemented via onFormValidateFlowConfig referencing a validation flow in flows[] — NOT via one-shot readOnly assignments inside onInitFlowConfig
The validation flow sets $form.toolbar.confirm.control.readOnly based on the computed validity of the current field values
The source-equals-destination rule pushes field-level errors via $validation.fieldErrors.<field_id>.push(...) onto both location fields
Every referenced flowId (onFormValidateFlowConfig.flowId, each clickFlowConfig.flowId, onInitFlowConfig.flowId if set) names a flow that actually exists in flows[]
No $form.<flowName>() call appears in flow code without a matching flow of that referenceName in flows[] (no phantom set_state-style calls)
The confirm flow assigns $form.outParams values and then calls $form.close()
All field ids and param ids are snake_case (e.g. source_location, destination_location, quantity)
configurationTypeId is 5 and referenceName eval_transfer_qty_form ends in _form; description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate form' run before 'dxs configuration upsert form'

evals.name: declarative-string-slots
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create eval_scoring_options_form with four fields: (1) a numeric weight field whose tooltip must convey exactly this: v2: higher score wins; tiebreak on smaller delta (2) a notes textBox with the placeholder Enter carrier notes (3) a cutoff date field displaying MM/DD/YYYY format (4) a read-only summary textBox whose initial value comes from the form's summary inParam. Confirm returns the weight and notes.
evals.expected_output: A form whose declarative string slots are correctly encoded as TypeScript expressions: the hazardous tooltip neutralized (no unwrapped semicolon/leading-colon), the textBox placeholder left as the plain-string exception, the format slot TS-quoted, and the inParam binding left as a raw unwrapped expression.
expectations: The weight field's tooltip is emitted as a TypeScript-expression string (backticks or a quoted TS string literal) — not bare unwrapped plain text, which would compile to broken tokens

The tooltip content neutralizes the documented breaking tokens: the leading 'v2:' bare-word label and the mid-sentence semicolon are either wrapped as a single-quoted TS string literal (e.g. "'v2, per...'" style) or rephrased — the raw 'v2: ...; ...' text is not left as an unwrapped expression

The notes textBox placeholder is treated as the documented plain-string exception: 'Enter carrier notes' appears as plain text with NO backtick or TS-quote wrapping (backticks would render literally in the UI)
The date field's format slot is a TS-quoted plain literal: "'MM/DD/YYYY'" (quotes inside the JSON string)
The summary field's value binding is the raw unwrapped expression "$form.inParams.summary" — no backticks, no quotes
No declarative string slot (value/tooltip/placeholder/format) in the final body contains an unwrapped mid-sentence semicolon, an unwrapped leading bare-word colon, or an unwrapped pipe
Sibling *Config keys are explicitly null on every controlConfig (only the active sub-config populated)
All param ids are snake_case; referenceName eval_scoring_options_form ends in _form; description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate form' run before 'dxs configuration upsert form'

evals.name: multi-select-field
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create eval_service_types_form where the user picks ONE OR MORE carrier service types — assume an existing selector eval_service_type_dd in the Utilities package backs the dropdown. Require at least one selection before Confirm enables, and return the selected list to the caller on confirm.
evals.expected_output: A form whose multi-choice field is a single selector-backed dropdown with allowMultiSelection: true producing an array value, at-least-one validation in the form-level validation flow, and an isCollection outParam — not a set of checkboxes.
expectations: The multi-choice field is a SINGLE selector-backed dropdown control with allowMultiSelection: true on its config — NOT a set of checkBox fields
The field's value is treated as an ARRAY of selector keys in flow code (the confirm flow emits the array, not a scalar)
The 'at least one selected' rule is validated in the form-level validation flow that gates the Confirm button — not via per-checkbox logic
The outParam carrying the selection is declared with isCollection: true and a snake_case id (e.g. service_types)
The selector reference on the field uses the target selector's package (Utilities) for its module reference — not the form's own feature/caller package
Confirm-button gating lives in onFormValidateFlowConfig + a validation flow setting $form.toolbar.confirm.control.readOnly
configurationTypeId is 5 and referenceName eval_service_types_form ends in _form; description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate form' run before 'dxs configuration upsert form'

evals.name: modify-existing-round-trip
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: two steps. Step 1 — create a minimal form eval_dock_note_form with a single note textBox and a Confirm button that returns the note to the caller. Step 2 — as a separate follow-up edit, add an optional priority number field (also returned to the caller on confirm) without disturbing the rest of the form.
evals.expected_output: An initial validated/upserted form, then a surgical round-trip modification (get envelope, extract inner .json, edit, re-validate, re-upsert) that adds the priority field and outParam while preserving the existing note field and confirm flow.
expectations: Step 1 runs 'dxs configuration validate form' before the initial 'dxs configuration upsert form'

The follow-up edit uses the round-trip: 'dxs configuration get form ... -O envelope.json' then extracts the inner body (jq .json envelope.json or equivalent) before editing — the envelope is NEVER fed directly to upsert
The edit is surgical: the existing note field, confirm toolbar button, and confirm flow are preserved (not rebuilt from scratch or dropped)
The new field id and outParam id are snake_case (priority)
The new priority outParam is declared required: false (it is optional and not written on the cancel path)
The outParams schema and the confirm flow's code are updated in the same edit (the flow writes $form.outParams.priority and the outParams array declares it — schema/code parity)
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate form' again before the second 'dxs configuration upsert form'
The form's description remains non-empty and at most 100 characters after the edit
